    Wakefulness-promoting agent · Schedule IV

    Modafinil Provigil

    Modafinil (Provigil) is a wakefulness-promoting medicine for excessive sleepiness from narcolepsy, obstructive sleep apnea, and shift work disorder. It is milder than amphetamines and a Schedule IV controlled substance. It can make hormonal birth control less effective.

    Modafinil at a glance

    Brand names
    Provigil; related armodafinil (Nuvigil)
    Drug class
    Wakefulness-promoting agent
    US legal status
    Schedule IV, prescription only
    Approved uses
    Excessive sleepiness from narcolepsy, obstructive sleep apnea, shift work disorder
    Forms
    Tablets
    Onset
    About 1 hour; peak 2 to 4 hours
    Half-life
    About 15 hours
    Broken down by
    Liver (CYP3A4); induces CYP3A4
    Key warning
    Serious rash; reduced birth control effectiveness

    What is modafinil used for?

    Modafinil is approved to improve wakefulness in adults with excessive sleepiness from narcolepsy, obstructive sleep apnea (alongside CPAP, not instead of it), and shift work disorder.[1]

    It is thought to work mainly by blocking dopamine reuptake, more weakly than stimulants, and by affecting other wake-promoting systems such as orexin and histamine.

    How is modafinil usually prescribed?

    The figures below come from the FDA-approved label and describe how prescribers typically use modafinil. They are not personal dosing advice. A prescriber sets the dose for each person and adjusts it over time.[1]

    ConditionTypical doseLabel guidance
    Narcolepsy, sleep apnea200 mg once in the morningDoses up to 400 mg showed no added benefit
    Shift work disorder200 mg about 1 hour before the shift
    Severe liver impairment100 mgHalf the usual dose

    What are the risks and side effects of modafinil?

    Common side effects include headache, nausea, nervousness, runny nose, back pain, diarrhea, anxiety, and insomnia.[1]

    Serious risks include rare but life-threatening skin reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), allergic reactions, psychiatric symptoms such as mania or psychosis, and chest pain or palpitations in people with heart disease.[1]

    Warning: Modafinil can make hormonal birth control, including pills, patches, rings, and implants, less effective during treatment and for one month after stopping. Use another method too.

    What should not be mixed with modafinil?

    Choose what it would be combined with:

    Combined withWhat happensLabel guidance
    Hormonal birth controlLower hormone levels; contraceptive failureUse backup contraception
    Cyclosporine, some HIV drugsLower levelsMonitor
    Omeprazole, diazepam, phenytoin (CYP2C19 substrates)Higher levelsMonitor
    MAOIsPossible interactionUse caution
    AlcoholNot well studiedAvoid

    This is not a full list. A pharmacist can check a complete medication list, including supplements and over-the-counter products.[1]

    What does modafinil overdose look like?

    Overdose causes insomnia, restlessness, agitation, confusion, anxiety, fast heartbeat, high blood pressure, and chest pain. Deaths from modafinil alone are rare.[1]

    If someone may be overdosing

    • Call 911 for chest pain, a seizure, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke (face drooping, weakness on one side, slurred speech), a very high body temperature, or if the person collapses.
    • Move them somewhere cool and calm, loosen tight clothing, and cool the skin with water. Do not try to hold them down.
    • If they become unresponsive or their breathing slows, give naloxone. Street stimulants are often contaminated with fentanyl.
    • For advice when the person is awake and stable, call Poison Help at 1-800-222-1222.

    What happens when you stop modafinil?

    Stopping modafinil does not usually cause withdrawal. Sleepiness returns. A few people feel tired or low for several days.[1]

    1. Day 1Sleepiness returnsThe underlying condition reappears.
    2. Days 2 to 7Possible fatigueMild tiredness or low mood in some people.
    3. OngoingTreat the causeCPAP, scheduled naps, and other treatments.

    How do you get modafinil legally in the US?

    In the United States, modafinil is a Schedule IV controlled substance. The only legal way to get it is with a prescription from a clinician registered with the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), filled by a licensed pharmacy. Depending on state law, that can be a physician, nurse practitioner, or physician assistant.[2]

    • Refills: a Schedule IV prescription can be refilled up to five times within six months of the date it was written. After that, a new prescription is needed.[3]
    • Telehealth: federal flexibilities let DEA-registered clinicians prescribe Schedule II to V medicines after a telemedicine visit, without a prior in-person exam, through December 31, 2026. A permanent DEA rule was under final review in late 2026. State rules can be stricter.[4]
    • Monitoring: prescribers and pharmacists in most states check a prescription drug monitoring program, a database of controlled-substance prescriptions, before prescribing or dispensing.
    • Pharmacies: a legitimate pharmacy always requires a valid prescription, has a licensed pharmacist available, and is licensed in the state it ships to. The FDA's BeSafeRx tool and the NABP's safe pharmacy list help confirm a pharmacy is real.[5][6]
    • Cost: generic modafinil is inexpensive; insurers often require a documented diagnosis.

    Traveling: keep the medicine in its original pharmacy container and carry a copy of the prescription. Check the rules of the destination country before travel, because many countries restrict controlled medicines or require a permit.

    Can you order modafinil online?

    Yes, but only with a valid prescription and only from a pharmacy licensed in your state. Many licensed pharmacies, including mail-order pharmacies run by insurers, fill modafinil prescriptions online and ship them. Buying modafinil from a website that does not require a prescription is illegal, and the product is often fake.[5][7]

    1. See a licensed clinicianA clinician evaluates you in person or by telemedicine and decides whether modafinil is appropriate.
    2. The prescription goes to a pharmacyPrescriptions for controlled medicines are usually sent electronically, straight from the prescriber to the pharmacy you choose.
    3. The pharmacy checks and fills itA pharmacist verifies the prescription and your identity, then dispenses the medicine in person or by mail.

    Signs that an online seller is illegal:

    • It sells modafinil with no prescription, or after only a short online questionnaire.
    • It takes orders through social media, messaging apps, or email.
    • It asks for payment in cryptocurrency, gift cards, or money transfers.
    • It has no US street address, no state pharmacy license, and no pharmacist to speak to.
    • Its prices are far below those of ordinary pharmacies, or it ships from another country.

    The FDA's BeSafeRx tool links to each state's license lookup, and the National Association of Boards of Pharmacy lists verified online pharmacies.[5][6]

    Is modafinil legal in other countries?

    CountryStatus
    United KingdomPrescription-only medicine; not a controlled drug

    Laws change and differ in detail. Check current rules before carrying any controlled medicine across a border.[8]

    Common questions about modafinil

    Is modafinil a stimulant?

    It promotes wakefulness and has mild stimulant-like effects, but it is weaker than amphetamines and has a lower risk of misuse.

    Is modafinil a "smart drug"?

    Studies in healthy, rested people show small effects on some tasks at best. Buying it without a prescription online is illegal and products may be counterfeit.

    Does modafinil affect birth control?

    Yes. It can make hormonal birth control fail during use and for a month after stopping.

    What is armodafinil?

    Armodafinil (Nuvigil) is the longer-lasting active half of modafinil, given at lower doses.
